rationale:
`assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md` is a bundled skill. It has front matter with `name: habeas`, so it is a site of `requirements.cli.skill_conventions`.

The requirement has one MUST: the description states when to use the skill in terms of the user's task. The `description` front matter does this. It opens with "Use at the start of any work in a project that tracks requirements with Habeas", then names concrete signals: a `habeas` dev-dependency, a `habeas.toml`, `{req}` directives, and `{impl}`/`{test}`/`{cite}` references. It also ties each other skill to a user task: design and any change go to habeas-requirements, moves go to habeas-refactor, validation findings go to habeas-evidence, and adoption goes to habeas-bootstrap-requirements. The trailing "Also the reference for directive and reference syntax, `habeas status` and `habeas info`…" adds more task-based use cases.

Naming other bundled skills is allowed by the MAY and imposes nothing to check. The description names them, and each name comes with the task it covers, so an agent can tell the skills apart.

There are no violation queries for this requirement. I found no gap.
